causalModel.founding: Greenspring was founded at the Panther fork. The springs there can be drunk unboiled.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The ground at the site is firm. Clean water rises at a stone lip. The site is the last dry footing before the Helstrom approach.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: The tribe is the last friendly stop in the interior. The tribe gives water away free. The tribe sells beds and rope at high prices.
causalModel.pressures: The Hist is sick. The villagers blame salt from upstream. Traffic on the Helstrom track brings cult couriers and factors. The tribe distrusts these visitors.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: If the spring soured, the village would have to move. The villagers would then need a new source of fresh water.

districts.notes: One common with the Hist, the spring and the landing.

why.what: Greenspring is a Hist village of seven buildings round an open common. The spring house stands on the bank. The landing on the bank is a set of beached canoes. The villagers have built no stage there.
why.whyHere: Clean water rises here. The site is the last dry ground before Helstrom.
why.whyNeighbours: Greenspring is the last friendly stop on the track to Helstrom. The refuge footpath runs along its bank.
why.playerPurpose: Beds and rope, free water and a trader are available in the village. The quests of the spring and the sick root start here.
why.microGeography: The slope falls west to the channel. The huts sit on mud pads. The Hist sits on a mound.

parcels.orientationWhy: The lodge door turns west to the common. It faces the way down to the spring.

playerPurpose.note: Beds rented to travellers on the Helstrom road, at a high price.
On market day, traders from the road fork set out their goods by the lodge door.

why.what: The lodge is the building where the bed-keeper rents beds and sells rope.
why.whyHere: The village lives by serving as the last friendly stop before Helstrom. Its income is the rent on its beds.
why.whySpot: The lodge stands on the first dry shelf that a traveller reaches from the track. It lies on the east side of the common.
why.whyNeighbours: The lodge faces the common across from the Hist shrine. The root-herald's house stands to the north.
why.playerPurpose: A bed for the night in a safe room is available at the lodge. Rope for the road is sold there.
why.microGeography: A mud pad is cut into the slope. The pad is graded down to the common.

parcels.orientationWhy: The root-herald's door turns south onto the common.

playerPurpose.note: The root-herald buys from travellers and sells what comes down from Helstrom.
The herald keeps the upriver salt that the village blames for the sick root.

why.what: The root-herald's house is the building where the village trades with Helstrom.
why.whyHere: The root-herald carries the trade of the village to Helstrom and back.
why.whySpot: The herald's house stands on the north edge of the common. It occupies the widest flat ground.
why.whyNeighbours: The herald's house looks across the common to the lodge and the Hist.
why.playerPurpose: The root-herald is a trader who keeps the salt. The salt starts the argument over the sick root.
why.microGeography: A mud pad lies on the north shelf. It stands above the wet ground by the water.

parcels.orientationWhy: The tree-minder's door turns north-west to the Hist and the shrine.

playerPurpose.note: The tree-minder can say what ails the Hist.

why.what: The tree-minder's house stands beside the Hist.
why.whyHere: A Hist village keeps its tree-minder close to the tree.
why.whySpot: The house stands on the rise east of the Hist. It is the nearest dry pad to the roots of the Hist.
why.whyNeighbours: The Hist and its shrine lie across the path to the west. The lodge lies to the north.
why.playerPurpose: The tree-minder speaks for the Hist. The tree-minder can start MR01.
why.microGeography: A mud pad is cut into the side of the rise of the Hist.

parcels.orientationWhy: The spring-keeper's door turns north to the spring house.

playerPurpose.note: The spring-keeper knows who uses the water and when it turned.

why.what: The spring-keeper's house stands above the spring.
why.whyHere: The spring-keeper and her family live beside the water that they keep.
why.whySpot: The house stands south of the spring house. It stands on the last dry ground before the bank.
why.whyNeighbours: The spring house lies below it to the north. The Hist stands up the slope to the east.
why.playerPurpose: The house is a home to enter. The spring-keeper is a witness for LH38.
why.microGeography: A mud pad lies on the low slope above the channel bank.

parcels.orientationWhy: The door of the family hut turns south-east to the common.

playerPurpose.note: Talk of the delegations that camped elsewhere (LH51).
A family that cooks for travellers and hears their talk.

why.what: A family hut stands on the west side of the common.
why.whyHere: The families of the village live round the common.
why.whySpot: The hut stands west of the herald's house. The ground there runs down to the water.
why.whyNeighbours: The hut faces the common. The herald's house lies to the east.
why.playerPurpose: The hut is a home to enter. The family there talks of the delegations that camped elsewhere.
why.microGeography: A mud pad lies on the gentle slope above the bank.

parcels.orientationWhy: The door of the north-east hut turns west toward the common and the herald's path.

playerPurpose.note: A family that sits out and watches who comes down the track.

why.what: A family hut stands on the north-east edge, by the track.
why.whyHere: The village has grown up the slope toward the track.
why.whySpot: The hut stands north of the lodge. It sits on a dry shelf beside the track.
why.whyNeighbours: The hut looks down the path to the common and the herald's house.
why.playerPurpose: The family there can say who came down the track and when.
why.microGeography: A mud pad is cut into the upper slope above the lodge.

parcels.orientationWhy: The open front of the spring house turns east to the path from the common.

playerPurpose.note: Boats from the river put in on the bank by the spring house.

why.what: The spring house is a roofed shelter over the stone lip where the water rises.
why.whyHere: The villagers founded the village on water that can be drunk unboiled.
why.whySpot: The spring house stands on the bank where the spring rises. It stands beside the footpath along the water.
why.whyNeighbours: The spring-keeper's house is just south. The landing lies north along the bank.
why.playerPurpose: Clean water is given free at the spring house. LH37 and LH38 both turn on this spring.
why.microGeography: The spring house stands on low ground above the channel bank, on a mud pad.

parcels.orientationWhy: The totems face the common, in front of the Hist.

playerPurpose.note: The Sick Root starts at the shrine at the foot of the Hist. The village blames salt from upstream for the dying tree.
The sick root lies beside the shrine. The cause lies in the flooded root-caves under the village.

why.what: The shrine at the foot of the Hist holds totems, candles and flowers.
why.whyHere: Argonian villages keep a shrine at the Hist. They build no temple.
why.whySpot: The shrine stands on the flat ground round the roots of the Hist. It faces the common.
why.whyNeighbours: The Hist is behind the shrine. The tree-minder's house lies across the path to the east.
why.playerPurpose: The shrine provides the shrine service. MR01 starts at the sick root.
why.microGeography: The mound of the Hist is levelled round its roots.

This route runs from the common to the lodge door.
This route runs from the common to the root-herald's door.
This route runs from the way to the family hut.
This route runs from the herald's path to the east family hut.
This route runs from the way to the tree-minder's door.
This route runs from the way to the spring house.
This route runs from the spring house up to the spring-keeper's door.
This route runs from the bank footpath down to the boats.
This route runs from the common to the shrine at the Hist.

landmarks.notes: The village's tribal Hist, ailing (MR01); hist-placement R2 tribal, R3 state sick.

why.what: The Hist of the village is a broad old tree. Its roots are sickening.
why.whyHere: Most Argonian tribes build round their Hist. This village was founded at the spring and its tree.
why.whySpot: The Hist stands on the mound above the common. The slope levels there before it falls to the water.
why.whyNeighbours: The shrine is at the foot of the Hist. The tree-minder's house stands beside it.
why.playerPurpose: Travellers see the Hist from the track. Its sick root is the subject of MR01.
why.microGeography: A raised mound of mud lies round the roots of the Hist. The mound stands on the slope above the channel.

approaches.sequence: A traveller comes down the track from the Border road. The crown of the Hist shows first over the trees. The lodge roof shows next. Then the smoke from the common shows.
approaches.wayfinding: The track ends at the top of the village. The way runs down past the tree-minder's house to the common.

approaches.sequence: A traveller walks up the footpath from the south-west. The spring house and the jars at its lip show first. The Hist shows above the spring house. The canoes on the bank show beyond it.
approaches.wayfinding: The footpath passes the spring house. The way up to the common leaves the footpath just past the spring.

networkTerminals.why: The track from the Border road comes down the ridge. It turns into the village at its east corner.
The footpath from the refuge comes up the channel bank. It enters the village at the spring house.

combatSpaces.why: The open common between the huts is the combat space. Any fight in the village takes place there.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: settlement-register row Greenspring (M3, a freshwater village at the fork); record npcs merchant (single) and family (band); notable slots tree-minder, root-herald, spring-keeper
scaleGrounding.why: Five households and the guests of the lodge live in the village. Seven buildings stand there, which are six houses and the spring house. They stand round one common with the Hist and the landing.

candidates.why: The first candidate is the west-facing slope between the end of the track and the channel bank. It has dry ground above the water. The refuge footpath runs along the bank.
The second candidate is the plotted anchor, at the end of the track from the Border road.
candidates.rejectedBecause: Slopes there run 6 to 10 degrees. The anchor lies 90 m from the water. The anchor leaves no room for a landing or the spring.
